channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: 8/1: STF contraria Moraes e abre precedente para descontar medidas cautelares das penas de réus
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) ruled, by six votes to four, to establish a precedent allowing precautionary measures applied to defendants in the January 8 acts to be deducted from their final sentences. The decision contradicts the earlier stance of Justice Alexandre de Moraes and may reduce prison time for those convicted of anti-democratic acts. The ruling sets a new parameter for penal execution in cases related to the January 8 events.

item.title: Caixa reúne entidades esportivas, cobra cumprimento dos contratos e mantém suspenso patrocínio à CBAt
item.description: Caixa Econômica Federal convened sports entities to demand strict compliance with sponsorship contracts after discovering that ex-athletes from the CBAt-sponsored Ídolos do Atletismo program posted social media content praising politicians Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio Bolsonaro and Tarcísio de Freitas while tagging the bank. The bank suspended sponsorship to CBAt and requested explanations, viewing the posts as potential breaches of institutional advertising rules using public funds during an election period.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro declara apoio à esposa de JHC ao Senado por Alagoas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro declared support for Marina Candia, wife of pre-candidate JHC, for the Senate in Alagoas, despite her being confirmed as a federal deputy candidate by the PSDB. The endorsement came after the PL nominated Alfredo Gaspar as its vice-presidential candidate, freeing up the Senate slot for Marina. The coalition between PSDB, PL, PDT and other parties remains undefined, with the second Senate seat expected to go to Arthur Lira (PP).

item.title: g1 e GloboNews entrevistam Ronaldo Caiado, candidato à Presidência pelo PSD
item.description: Goiás Governor Ronaldo Caiado, the PSD's presidential candidate, will be interviewed by g1 and GloboNews on Monday at 2 p.m. in a live, simultaneous broadcast by journalists Andréia Sadi and Natuza Nery. He is the third candidate to be interviewed in the series, following Renan Santos and Romeu Zema, while Lula declined the invitation and Flávio Bolsonaro has not yet responded. The interview is part of an invitation extended to the five top candidates in the July 24 Datafolha poll.

item.title: TSE cria conselho para monitorar IA e desinformação nas eleições
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has established the Advisory Council on Informational Integrity for the 2026 Elections to monitor risks linked to artificial intelligence and disinformation, aiming to safeguard the legitimacy and normal functioning of the electoral process. The body will advise the Court's presidency on informational integrity measures.

item.title: Os desencontros da chapa presidencial bolsonarista
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto and Flávio Bolsonaro disagree on when Alfredo Gaspar was chosen as vice-presidential candidate, with Flávio stating the idea came at the last minute. Flávio said he preferred Daniella Marques as his running mate but is satisfied with Gaspar, leaving open the possibility of Gaspar returning to the Senate race. The PL party’s internal resolution in Alagoas confirms Gaspar could run for Senate if he steps down from the vice-presidential ticket.

item.title: PF vai convocar ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula para depor sobre repasses de lobista
item.description: The Federal Police has summoned former Chief of Staff to President Lula, Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (known as Marcola), to testify in two investigations before the Supreme Federal Court (STF) involving lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger and Flávio Luís Lula da Silva, the president's eldest son. The inquiries concern alleged irregular payments linked to lobbying activities. The article is available exclusively to subscribers.

item.title: Zema propõe prisão preventiva de ‘criminoso contumaz’
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential candidate for 2026, proposed in his government plan that individuals detained three times should be subject to preventive detention. The measure primarily targets low-level offenses such as theft and robbery, aiming to reduce recidivism through stricter enforcement of pre-trial detention.

item.title: O que motivou Dino a mandar PF investigar novas irregularidades em emendas
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino ordered the Federal Police to investigate potential crimes linked to irregularities in individual amendments (Pix amendments), following a TCU report identifying R$ 55 million in losses across 100 amendments. The irregularities included lack of transparency, unverified payments, and overbilling, indicating persistent unconstitutionality in the execution of these funds.

item.title: Toffoli nega pedido que permitiria candidatura de desafeto de Moro
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Dias Toffoli rejected a petition by former state deputy Tony Garcia to annul a civil non-prosecution agreement that bars him from running for public office for eight years, stemming from Operation Rádio Patrulha. Garcia argued the decision should be extended by analogy to the annulment of cases against former governor Beto Richa, but Toffoli denied the request, stating the legal grounds do not automatically apply. Even if successful, Garcia would not be guaranteed candidacy, as his party, the Christian Democracy, has opted to support Sergio Moro in the Paraná gubernatorial race.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: O vice problemático de Flávio e os humildes bens de Erika Hilton
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program discusses Flávio Bolsonaro’s vice-presidential pick, highlighting controversies around the choice, while also covering Erika Hilton’s modest asset declaration and Romeu Zema’s government plan. It further examines the PT’s criticism of Alfredo Gaspar and other relevant political news.

item.title: Casa JOTA reúne campanhas presidenciais para debater agenda digital
item.description: Casa JOTA in Brasília will host representatives from the main presidential campaigns on Wednesday, August 12, at 9 a.m., in an event sponsored by Brasscom. The goal is to hear each candidate's priorities regarding Brazil's digital development, based on the 'Digital Agenda: Proposals for the 2027-2030 Cycle' document prepared by Brasscom. The event will be livestreamed on JOTA's YouTube channel and fully covered across all JOTA platforms.

item.title: O que a PGR disse a Moraes sobre a foto de Daniel Silveira com senador
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (PGR) submitted an opinion to the STF advocating that Daniel Silveira remain in open regime, but with new 'guidelines' to prevent social media access, following a video in which he supported Senator Carlos Portinho's re-election bid. The PGR views the incident as isolated and emphasizes the rehabilitative purpose of penal execution, warning that future violations will not be tolerated. Minister Alexandre de Moraes will decide Silveira's fate, as the opinion is non-binding.

item.title: TSE cria órgão para monitorar fake news e uso indevido de IA nas eleições
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has established the Advisory Council on Informational Integrity to monitor false content and the improper use of artificial intelligence in the 2026 elections. Composed of unpaid experts in technology, public security, and communications, the council will advise TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques, propose partnerships, and promote digital literacy. Meetings will be held at least monthly until December.

item.title: Erika Hilton declara ter patrimônio 20% menor que em 2022
item.description: Federal deputy Erika Hilton (PSOL) declared assets of R$15,975.73 to the TSE in 2026, 20.08% lower than the R$19,989.96 declared in 2022. The majority of her current assets are held in a Caixa Econômica Federal checking account (R$13,602.14), followed by fixed-income investments (Nubank, Tesouro Direto, and RDB). She is the first Black transgender woman to lead a congressional bench in Brazil and is running for re-election in São Paulo.

item.title: João Campos tem patrimônio quase oito vezes maior que Raquel Lyra
item.description: The national president of the PSB and former mayor of Recife, João Campos, declared a net worth of R$2.8 million to electoral authorities — nearly eight times that of Governor Raquel Lyra, according to filings with the TSE. This wealth disparity has become a notable point of comparison in the 2026 Pernambuco gubernatorial race, sparking discussion on candidate transparency and economic inequality.

item.title: Em plano de governo, Zema propõe privatizar Petrobras e freio ao STF
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) proposed in his government plan the privatization of all state-owned enterprises, including Petrobras and public banks, reducing the age of criminal responsibility to 16 years, limiting the power of the STF with a minimum age of 60 for justices and ending senators' privileged jurisdiction, alongside labor flexibilization and state reduction. The program also includes PPPs in health and education, visa exemptions for tourists from safe countries, and regulation of homeschooling.

item.title: TSE realiza sessão extraordinária virtual entre os dias 12 e 14 de agosto
item.description: The TSE convened an extraordinary virtual session from August 12 to 14 to review referendums on preliminary measures and urgent injunctions, allowing oral arguments by lawyers for up to five minutes. The list of cases to be judged will be available on the TSE's 'Pautas de Julgamento' page, as published in the Electronic Justice Diary. File formats and size limits for attachments in the PJe system follow TSE Ordinance No. 886/2017.

item.title: Kalil declara R$ 5,9 milhões em bens ao TSE; 62% a mais que em 2022
item.description: Former Belo Horizonte mayor Alexandre Kalil (PDT), candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, declared R$ 5.9 million in assets to the TSE for the 2026 elections, a 62% increase from the R$ 3.65 million declared in 2022. The growth of approximately R$ 2.2 million over four years is driven by an apartment valued at R$ 1.85 million and a foreign bank deposit of R$ 1.42 million. Kalil was the first candidate for governor of Minas to officially register his candidacy in this electoral cycle.

item.title: Lula usa ministros para tentar atrair André Mendonça para a arena política
item.description: Lula's allies used meetings with Minister André Mendonça to politically pressure him in the investigations against Lulinha, attempting to drag the case into the political arena and disqualify his rulings. The strategy included spreading suspicions, creating leak narratives, and even changing STF jurisprudence to assign two rapporteurs to the same case, including Flávio Dino. The meeting mediated by Jorge Messias at the TSE was framed as a 'conciliation,' but it actually served to spread rumors of pacification and give Lula the narrative that he supports regular investigations.

item.title: PT aciona TSE contra plataforma do PL por “conteúdos mentirosos” contra Lula
item.description: The PT, together with PCdoB and PV, filed a representation with the TSE against the platform 'direitaja.com', linked to the PL, accusing it of spreading false content, deep fakes, and negative electoral propaganda against President Lula on a large scale. The Brazil of Hope federation claims the site is being used as a tool for electoral disinformation harmful to Lula's re-election campaign.

item.title: Início da campanha deve trazer duas tendências para corrida presidencial
item.description: The official start of the electoral campaign on August 16 is expected to benefit lesser-known opposition candidates — Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos, and Romeu Zema — who currently poll below 15% combined but have significant growth potential due to increased visibility. The second trend is the possible reversal of Lula’s recent decline in polls, as Brazilian presidents seeking re-election historically see improved approval ratings in the six months before the first round, though this depends on voter mobilization and perceptions of governability.

item.title: Dino manda PF investigar indícios de crimes em emendas Pix apontados pelo TCU; repasse feito por vice de Flávio está na lista
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino referred the TCU audit to the Federal Police, which identified indications of crimes in Pix amendments, with estimated losses of R$ 49.1 million between 2020 and 2024, including a R$ 6.2 million transfer by deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), vice-presidential running mate of Flávio Bolsonaro, to São José da Laje (AL), where funds could not be traced. The audit found irregularities in 82% of the transfers and lack of mandatory reporting in the Transferegov system.

item.title: TSE cria conselho para acompanhar desinformação e uso de inteligência artificial
item.description: The TSE has established the Advisory Council on Informational Integrity for the 2026 Elections to advise the Presidency on combating disinformation and the misuse of artificial intelligence. The multidisciplinary, consultative body will bring together experts from ten strategic fields—including technology, public security, communications, and electoral law—to safeguard the legitimacy and normalcy of the electoral process.

item.title: Ministro da Justiça se reúne com Mendonça em busca de distensionar crise com PF
item.description: Justice Minister Wellington César met with STF Minister André Mendonça and Attorney General Jorge Messias to ease tensions between the Federal Police and the judiciary over investigations involving Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Lulinha. The meeting aimed to create a technical communication channel to improve coordination and de-escalate the conflict, particularly regarding delays in the Master Bank and INSS investigations.

item.title: Sem convite de presidenciáveis, dono da Multi volta foco ao Ranking dos Políticos
item.description: Businessman Alexandre Ostrowiecki, owner of Multi and founder of the Political Ranking platform, has not received invitations to collaborate with 2026 presidential campaigns and is focusing on his initiative that evaluates lawmakers based on their commitment to fighting privilege, corruption, and waste of public funds. He states his goal is to improve the quality of Brazil's Congress.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Planos de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro para a economia têm reta final de definições
item.description: Economic plans from Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro for the 2026 election are becoming more defined after behind-the-scenes talks with financial market operators. Flávio Bolsonaro’s team detailed a spending cut equivalent to 1.5% of GDP (over R$200 billion), focusing on gradual reduction of the public workforce while maintaining full replacement in essential services like security. Meanwhile, Lula’s team has ruled out including free public transportation in their platform.

item.title: A ofensiva da esquerda no TSE contra plataforma ligada ao PL
item.description: The PT, PV, and PCdoB party federation has filed a request with the TSE to investigate the 'Direita Já' platform, linked to the PL party, for allegedly misusing Public Party Fund resources to spread false content, deepfakes, and digital attacks against President Lula. The complaint states the platform produces around 50 weekly publications, partners with over 200 influencers, and reaches up to 50 million views, constituting a possible diversion of public funds for disinformation purposes. The parties are demanding the removal of illegal content and greater transparency regarding the contracts and payments sustaining the platform’s operations.

item.title: Crusoé: Escândalo do INSS chega à antessala de Lula
item.description: The scandal involving irregularities in the INSS is reaching the presidential inner circle, raising concerns in Lula's government over the risk of associating power with figures linked to corruption. In an election year, such a narrative can be especially damaging, as it fuels perceptions of proximity between the government core and illegal practices, even without direct proof of Lula's involvement.

item.title: PL de Alagoas mantém porta aberta para Alfredo Gaspar disputar o Senado
item.description: The Alagoas state leadership of the PL approved a mechanism allowing federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar to run for the Senate, despite his official nomination as vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s ticket. The decision, made just hours after the presidential ticket announcement, preserves an alternative for the state election.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro correm para fazer pente-fino na vida de Alfredo Gaspar
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar, selected as Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate in the 2026 presidential race, is undergoing an internal vetting by the campaign due to allegations of rape of a vulnerable person and misappropriation of parliamentary amendments. The Bolsonaro team fears undetected scandals could harm Flávio’s candidacy, though allies argue Gaspar provides strategic value by leveraging INSS CPMI material against the Lula government.

item.title: TSE: PT questiona uso do fundo partidário em plataforma de direita
item.description: The PT-PV-PCdoB Federation filed a complaint with the TSE against the platform direitaja.com, created by the PL, alleging improper use of the Partisan Fund to spread disinformation, deepfakes, and negative propaganda against Lula, including false associations with the PCC and drug trafficking. The parties argue the platform operates as a parallel coordination mechanism to circumvent electoral transparency and boost rules, achieving artificially amplified reach. They demand an investigation into the financial origins and immediate removal of content already identified as disinformation.

item.title: Abrindo a porta do governo
item.description: The text argues that fighting corruption in Brazil requires more than police operations and delayed judicial rulings; it demands opening the budget process to direct citizen control by those who pay taxes. It criticizes the traditional top-down, technocratic model of governance that favors elites and inflated mega-projects, and denounces 'false participation' as a tactic to appease public demand for transparency.

item.title: Sob o fogo da diplomacia Donroe
item.description: Trump and Milei allegedly participated in a White House-coordinated operation to support Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil's 2026 elections, acting as high-profile campaign surrogates. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin criticized the foreign interference, stating that presidents should not involve themselves in other countries' elections.

item.title: Lei Maria da Penha completa 20 anos: o que mudou na legislação e por que mulheres ainda continuam morrendo
item.description: The Maria da Penha Law marked its 20th anniversary with significant advances in protecting women, including classifying domestic violence crimes as unconditionally public prosecution, implementing more humanized police procedures, and enabling faster protective measures. Despite these improvements, feminicides in Brazil reached 1,571 cases in 2025—the highest in historical series—highlighting ongoing challenges in law enforcement and gender-based violence prevention. The issue became central in the 2026 electoral campaigns, with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro emphasizing the fight against feminicide in their speeches.

item.title: Zema lança plano com ataque ao STF, privatizações e saída do BRICS
item.description: Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema (Novo) launched the 'Implacable Plan' alongside Eduardo Girão as running mate, proposing attacks on the Supreme Court, extensive privatizations, and withdrawal from BRICS. The program characterizes Brazil as a 'stolen country' by a political and institutional elite, advocating a radical liberal agenda of minimal state.

item.title: Lula desarma pauta-bomba do PT na economia e deve indicar contenção de gastos obrigatórios em programa de governo
item.description: Lula’s economic team successfully neutralized fiscally risky internal PT proposals — such as zero-fare public transport, privatization reversals, and capital controls — removing them from the 2026 government program. The president endorsed explicit mention of spending restraint on mandatory expenditures and reinforced fiscal consolidation signals, aligned with the 2027 LDO, which targets a primary surplus in 2025 and a two-percentage-point-of-GDP fiscal adjustment by 2030. While universalizing full-time schooling (estimated at R$ 170 billion over 10 years) remains a goal, it will be budget-constrained, with the program avoiding detailed targets to preserve flexibility for electoral and governance phases.

item.title: Fator Lulinha: o dia em que a PF suspeitou de negócios do filho do presidente
item.description: President Lula's son, Fábio Luís, known as Lulinha, is under investigation for alleged business dealings with government-linked entrepreneurs, creating political vulnerability for the president in an election year. The Federal Police highlights a pattern of suspicious connections, including a 2008 incident in Foz do Iguaçu where Lulinha received VIP treatment at Itaipu Binacional and dined in Argentina with the company's president. The situation raises concerns about conflicts of interest and potential damage to the government's image.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vai gravar vídeos específicos para diferentes grupos de evangélicos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign is producing customized videos for different evangelical denominations, using specific greetings and themes to appeal to each group, after a Quaest poll showed a technical tie with Lula (PT) among evangelical voters (35% vs 28%, 4-point margin of error). The effort includes meetings with leaders from churches such as Ministério de Madureira, Igreja Universal do Reino de Deus, and Igreja Mundial do Poder de Deus, aiming to strengthen support in a segment where Bolsonaro previously led in July (39% vs 26%).

item.title: O bloqueio das contas de ex-ministro de Bolsonaro
item.description: Former minister Fábio Faria had his bank accounts blocked by the TSE for failing to pay a 30,000-real fine, now updated to 52,000 reais, for distorting a statement by then-candidate Lula during a 2023 debate. He was sanctioned in the same case that also punished Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Deputy Bia Kicis, who have already paid their fines. The account seizure and inclusion in the federal public sector’s delinquent credit registry followed his March edict summons and non-payment.

item.title: Crusoé: Flávio aponta os responsáveis pela escolha de um vice homem
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) blamed the Centrão bloc for the selection of a male running mate in the presidential ticket, despite his preference for a female candidate. He pointed to Deputy Alfredo Gaspar, rapporteur of the INSS CPMI and pre-candidate for Senate in Alagoas, as the chosen vice-presidential nominee. The statement was made in an interview with Crusoé and republished by O Antagonista.

item.title: Alfredo Gaspar supera 100 mil buscas no Google após ser anunciado como vice de Flávio Bolsonaro, aponta levantamento
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar, federal deputy from PL-Alagoas, surpassed 100,000 Google Brazil searches within 24 hours after being announced as the vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) ticket for the 2026 elections. The surge in public interest highlights the political impact of the Bolsonaro-aligned coalition’s formation on the electoral agenda.

item.title: Um plano do PT para evitar fiasco com Lula em estádio
item.description: The PT is planning to mobilize supporters from other states, including Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Paraná, to attend Lula's campaign launch event at the 1º de Maio stadium in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), fearing low turnout. The venue is considered Lula's political birthplace, but there are concerns about initial attendance for the campaign.

item.title: Lula resgata velha estratégia para tentar se afastar do escândalo de lobby de Lulinha
item.description: President Lula reportedly feels betrayed by PT ministers who initially denied knowledge of his son Fábio Luís Lula da Silva’s (Lulinha) lobbying activities in government ministries. According to allies, Lula now believes the aides lied when they claimed they did not assist Lulinha in business dealings. His defense strategy remains unchanged: asserting ignorance of his son’s actions, repeating a pattern seen in past scandals.

item.title: Flávio ataca Lula por Milei e tenta abafar fiasco do vice
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro issued a manifesto opposing the Lula government's decision to downgrade diplomatic relations with Argentina, aiming to divert attention from the failure in selecting Alfredo Gaspar as his running mate. The move was analyzed as a tactical effort to create a 'smokescreen' to overshadow the PL's isolation, lack of Centrão support, and backlash over Gaspar's nomination, which also advances Arthur Lira's local interests in Alagoas.

item.title: Governo tenta reduzir tensão da PF com gabinete de André Mendonça, mas impasse permanece
item.description: The Brazilian government is attempting to ease tensions between the Federal Police and Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça over information flow in the INSS and Master case investigations. While meetings between the AGU, Justice Minister, and Mendonça have smoothed relations and scheduled a follow-up with PF Director Andrei Rodrigues, Federal Police sources say the core legal impasse remains, as judicial restrictions on investigative progress continue to challenge PF autonomy and could jeopardize the validity of future acts.

item.title: 'Fora da bolha': O GLOBO lança 1º episódio de videocast com análises e bastidores da campanha eleitoral de 2026
item.description: O GLOBO launched the first episode of its weekly videocast 'Fora da Bolha', featuring newsroom journalists analyzing the behind-the-scenes and key themes of the 2026 Brazilian election campaign. The inaugural episode covered the investigation into Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), the latest Genial/Quaest poll, Alfredo Gaspar’s designation as Flávio Bolsonaro’s running mate, Donald Trump’s influence on Brazilian politics, and Senator Cleitinho’s shifting stance on running for governor of Minas Gerais.

item.title: Os bastidores da despedida de Marcola da campanha de Lula
item.description: Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, resigned from Lula’s campaign after being questioned about a R$249,000 payment received from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger. Before stepping down, he called President Lula and PT national president Edinho Silva, blaming internal party conflicts — describing them as 'friendly fire' — for his departure. Lula and Edinho publicly defended him, downplaying the controversy.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Fernando Haddad criticized the selection of Alfredo Gaspar as vice on Flávio Bolsonaro’s ticket, calling it one of the worst choices imaginable and questioning the audacity of appointing someone so unqualified to the position.

item.title: Tarcísio coloca ‘prosperidade’ como eixo central de plano de governo para a reeleição
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) has made 'prosperity' the central theme of his 2026 re-election government plan, centered around the SuperAção program, which currently supports 105,000 families and aims to expand to 200,000 by 2027. The plan, featuring ten strategic objectives including security, health, and education, will be filed with the TSE on July 7 and detailed on August 15. Tarcísio has revised his stance on privatizations, stating that private management does not always outperform the public sector, citing the temporary reassumption of CPTM operations after repeated failures by Trivia Trens, including service suspensions and a train fire.
